overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body responsible for setting policy, approving budgets, and directing educational leadership for the Medford Public Schools district. The archive spans 127 meetings held between September 2022 and October 2026. Across this period, the committee managed district leadership transitions, capital facility repairs, school construction eligibility, budget overrides, and policy revisions. As of the most recent meeting, the committee selected a ground-source geothermal HVAC system for Missituk Elementary, approved a Construction Manager at Risk delivery model for Roberts Elementary repairs, and received a first-quarter financial update.

threads.name: MSBA Core Program and High School Building Project
threads.summary: The committee initiated efforts to rebuild Medford High School by approving a Statement of Interest to the Massachusetts School Building Authority (MSBA) Core Program in April 2023 (M18#6) and securing acceptance into the eligibility phase (M37#5). The body established the High School Building Committee in early 2024 (M42#7), entered a formal feasibility study agreement in February 2025 (M78#7), and selected Left Field as Owner's Project Manager (M86#5). In February 2026, the committee approved the project's educational plan (M103#3). Feasibility studies led to narrowing design options, including adjusting building plans to navigate a 1967 DCR deed restriction on Edgerly Field (M115#2). In July 2026, the committee set sustainability targets while submitting an updated Chapter 74 viability form for MSBA review (M122#7).

threads.name: School Facilities Infrastructure and HVAC Upgrades
threads.summary: Facing severe district-wide cooling and heating failures (M29#6), the committee approved a $15 to $20 million partial-decarbonization HVAC replacement scope for the Andrews and McGlynn middle schools in April 2024 (M49#6). The committee authorized a $5 million initial bond request in December 2024 (M74#6), followed by approval of a $25.77 million total bond request in April 2025 (M83#7). Turning to elementary facilities, the body approved a $22.7 million schematic design for HVAC electrification and roof replacement at Roberts Elementary School in August 2026 (M123#4). The committee also authorized a Construction Manager at Risk model for Roberts Elementary and selected a ground-source geothermal HVAC system for Missituk Elementary in October 2026 (M127#4).

threads.name: Elementary School Overcrowding and Space Utilization
threads.summary: To address severe capacity shortages at Roberts Elementary School (M60#8), the committee initiated a district-wide elementary overcrowding review in April 2025 (M84#4). The body took initial action by relocating preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk Elementary in June 2025 (M89#6). Following a space utilization study, the committee gathered public feedback on proposed middle school reconfiguration models (M99#5) before voting in July 2026 to defer any middle school grade configuration changes to the 2028-2029 school year (M122#4). In October 2026, the committee evaluated a proposed elementary school reassignment policy to manage placement requests (M126#5).

threads.name: Before and After School Programming Expansion
threads.summary: The committee continuously addressed waitlists and capacity constraints in before- and after-school care (M09#4). In March 2023, the body transitioned the waitlist for incoming kindergartners to an on-demand lottery (M16#5). To support expansion, the committee partnered with the Belmont After School Enrichment Collaborative (BASIC) in May 2025 (M87#2) and transitioned site coordinators to full-time roles in August 2025 (M92#3). Based on BASIC recommendations, the committee approved adding 150 program seats and adopting a flexible tuition rate card in May 2026 (M113#4). By October 2026, the administration reported a 50 percent increase in enrollment and significant waitlist reductions (M127#3).

threads.name: Superintendent Evaluation and Leadership Transitions
threads.summary: The committee evaluated Superintendent Dr. Marice Edouard-Vincent using official state performance metrics (M23#6). Following contract negotiations, Dr. Edouard-Vincent announced her departure, prompting the committee to appoint Assistant Superintendent Dr. Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent in December 2024 (M73#2), approving her employment contract in January 2025 (M75#3). After conducting an evaluation of Interim Superintendent Galusi's performance (M102#6), the committee voted in February 2026 to appoint her as permanent superintendent (M103#4). The body subsequently finalized a three-year contract with Superintendent Galusi in May 2026 (M113#6).

threads.name: District Operating Budget and Supplemental Override Allocation
threads.summary: After addressing mid-year budget shortfalls in early 2024 (M41#4), the committee approved an operating budget of $77.75 million for FY25 (M55#7). The body voted to support local tax override ballot questions 7 and 8 in September 2024 (M62#8), and later allocated the voter-approved override revenues in a January 2025 supplemental budget to restore staffing and reserves (M75#7). In early 2026, joint meetings with the City Council addressed a projected $5 million gap required for level services (M107#5), leading to the approval of the FY27 operating budget in June 2026 (M120#4). The committee reviewed first-quarter financial status and risk management in October 2026 (M127#6).

threads.name: Career and Technical Education Development and Admissions
threads.summary: The committee monitored growth in vocational programs at Medford Vocational Technical High School, securing state grant funding for shop equipment (M02#3). The body requested that CTE expansion options be incorporated into the high school building feasibility study (M51#8). In October 2025, the committee adopted a lottery admissions policy for oversubscribed Chapter 74 programs (M95#3), which was later updated to incorporate state guidance (M110#3). The committee approved an updated Chapter 74 viability form for the high school building project in July 2026 (M121#1) and received a presentation on an honors pilot for vocational students in September 2026 (M124#4).

threads.name: School Climate, Discipline, and Safety Protocols
threads.summary: Following student safety incidents and public concern, the committee requested a climate assessment at the high school in November 2022 (M06#8) and adopted a 10-point safety plan in January 2023 (M11#5). Educational consultant Michael Welch presented recommendations on security and climate in May 2023 (M20#7). In late 2024, the committee approved capital funding for high school bathroom vape detectors and security cameras (M72#9). The body approved updated restraint and bullying prevention policies in May 2026 (M114#6), and clarified handbook rules regarding academic honesty appeals and prohibitions on withholding recess as discipline (M120#6).

The body also selected a new elementary literacy curriculum and established policies for facility naming and bullying prevention.
